items.reasons: B makes the local-contract rule and coordinator boundary explicit while retaining the documented installer attribution and root-writing scope. A is compatible with the evidence but omits the installer and root-guidance boundary, leaving both clients more to infer. B does not instruct the coordinator to change native actions. The receipt confirms validation and unchanged actions; the installer description comes from AGENTS.md. This favors behavioral completeness, not style.

sources.quote:
Project-readiness inspected the enclosing public worktree. Its installer writes
worktree-root guidance and actions, so this bounded application retains the
reviewable nested contract for the coordinator to integrate without modifying
the enclosing repository's native actions.
One coordinator integrates. Writing workers need separate worktrees and bounded file ownership.
"nested_project_contract": "validated against installed project-readiness contract validator; enclosing worktree actions not modified"
Claude responds well to clear, explicit instructions.
It can be more sensitive to instructions contained in skills and other files, such as `AGENTS.md`.
